Horticalc 0.6.2 replaces the fragile external-browser launcher with a native
desktop host and hardens the portable application lifecycle on Windows and
Linux. The calculation engine, FastAPI service, data formats, and portable
`user/` directory remain compatible.

## Why the launcher changed

The previous launcher had to discover Edge, Chrome, or Chromium, start a
foreign browser in app mode, track browser processes and temporary profiles,
and infer application shutdown from PIDs and timing. That model could behave
differently on clean Windows installations and made browser startup state part
of Horticalc's reliability.

Horticalc now owns one native pywebview window. It still serves the existing UI
and API locally, but uses WebView2 on Windows and GTK/WebKitGTK on Linux as the
system rendering runtime. Closing the native window now owns server shutdown.
There is no external browser detection, browser tab, temporary Chromium
profile, browser-PID supervision, or browser fallback.

## Desktop lifecycle and hardening

- A second launch restores and activates the existing single window instead of
  starting another server or window.
- The instance lock records the owning PID, port, start time, and a random
  activation token. The private local activation endpoint authenticates every
  request and is hidden from the public API schema.
- The server binds only to `127.0.0.1` and accepts the expected local hosts.
- The desktop host exposes no general JavaScript-to-Python bridge, disables
  external navigation and downloads, and serves the UI with a restrictive
  Content Security Policy.
- Windows explicitly uses WebView2. There is no MSHTML/Internet Explorer, Qt,
  CEF, bundled Chromium, or ordinary-browser fallback.
- Startup failures and native-window close share centralized cleanup so the
  server and instance lock do not survive the desktop process.

## Linux packaging and support

The Linux package now treats GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1 as one coherent system
runtime. It no longer mixes bundled Ubuntu copies of GLib, GTK, ICU, or
`libstdc++` with WebKitGTK from the target machine. Bundle verification rejects
those system libraries as well as accidental Qt, CEF, or Chromium renderers.

The packaged GUI lifecycle is tested on Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13,
and Fedora 44. Linux Mint 22.3 is a manual VM gate. Other distributions are
best effort, and Linux releases are currently x86_64 only.

Install the required system runtime before starting Horticalc:

```bash
# Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 13, Linux Mint 22.3
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y libgirepository-1.0-1 gir1.2-webkit2-4.1

# Fedora 44
sudo dnf install -y webkit2gtk4.1
```

Horticalc never invokes `sudo` or installs these packages automatically. If the
runtime is absent, it exits cleanly and prints the appropriate command.

## Profile and calculation workflow

- Target profiles can save and load their Solver setup through one explicit
  checkbox. Leaving it unchecked loads only the nutrient targets, so the
  current Solver configuration is preserved.
- User-created recipes and Solver target profiles can now be deleted in the
  GUI. Shipped entries remain protected; deleting a user override reveals the
  shipped entry again.
- Tiny floating-point residue is normalized out of calculated results instead
  of surfacing as meaningless near-zero nutrient values.
- Water-analysis terminology and translations were refined.
- The shipped recipe set was reduced to transparent reference recipes, and
  obsolete Solver research/matrix tooling was removed from the product tree.

## Verification

- The complete automated test suite covers the API, calculation engine,
  frontend, single-instance behavior, launcher cleanup, and packaging rules.
- Packaged Windows and Linux applications receive build and headless smoke
  tests.
- The native Linux GUI matrix verifies window discovery, second-launch
  activation, restore/focus behavior, native close, server shutdown, and lock
  cleanup on all four automated distributions.
- The native desktop flow was manually verified on clean Windows 10 and
  Windows 11 VMs, with and without Chrome affecting the environment.

Windows native GUI automation remains a future hardening step; Windows 10 and Windows 11
are currently the required manual desktop gates. Windows 7, Windows
8/8.1, and macOS are not supported.

## Upgrade notes

- Windows requires a current Microsoft WebView2 Runtime. It is normally present
  on supported Windows 10/11 systems and is not bundled or installed by
  Horticalc.
- Source checkouts need the desktop dependencies declared by the project; use
  `python -m pip install -e .` if pywebview is missing.
- `HORTICALC_NO_GUI=1` is the headless server mode. The obsolete
  `HORTICALC_NO_BROWSER` and `HORTICALC_KEEP_SERVER` variables were removed and
  have no compatibility aliases.
- Existing profiles, preferences, recipes, and the portable `user/` directory
  remain in place. As before, extract the release to a writable directory and
  back up `user/` before replacing an older portable build.

Release archives include SHA-256 checksum files and GitHub Artifact
Attestations. They provide integrity and build-provenance verification, but the
Windows executable is not Authenticode-signed.
